items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I had a next door neighbor -- a young lady, her name I remember her name vividly, her name was Pat Bolen, Patricia Bolen

ctx.x: As I sit here and reminisce and look over some of my notes, I find myself becoming interested in how I got into jazz so deeply as a young man. But during 1928 to '30 when

I was in high school, I had a next door neighbor -- a young lady, her name I remember her name vividly, her name was Pat Bolen, Patricia Bolen -- and in the summer, I would practice in my room with an open window, and I would hear this music, and she had every Top Five, Louis Armstrong Top Five record to date at that time -- and this was '28 and '29, and of course back in New England, that was unusual to hear that kind of music.

And I had that coming in my ears day and night. She used to help her mother in the kitchen; she used to have an old crank phonograph and she used to play everything -- and I would hear 'Sleepy Time Down South' and 'Cornet Chop Suey' and a whole array of all the songs that Louie first made, and that was my first intro to jazz along with the bands that I heard, which we already discussed -- at the old Beach and the playing of the colleges in my home town.
